O.content: The title includes "Midyear Months," and the visible point labels are May, June, July, August, and September.
No points or labels for months outside May through September are visible.
No visible mark or inscription states a causal effect, return on investment, profitability threshold, or approval criterion.

B.text: If a broader budget increase requires full-year performance evidence or evidence beyond a descriptive midyear association, then a dashboard limited to labeled midyear months does not satisfy that requirement; the appropriate follow-up is to hold and request full-year marketing analysis.
B.conditions: Applies only if the budget decision standard requires full-year analysis or causal, profitability, or other unshown validation; no such standard is supplied in the task.

O.content: The title visibly reads "Midyear Months with Strong Response: Ad Spend vs Sales".
The horizontal-axis inscription reads "Advertising Spend ($ thousands)" and has labeled ticks from 25 through 75.
The vertical-axis inscription reads "Sales ($ thousands)" and has labeled ticks from 70 through 180.
The points labeled May, June, July, August, and September appear successively farther right and higher on the page.

B.text: If the horizontal axis encodes Advertising Spend ($ thousands), the vertical axis encodes Sales ($ thousands), and the labeled monthly points are comparable observations, then points progressing rightward and upward indicate a positive midyear association between spend and sales. Approving a broader budget increase follows only if this association is accepted as sufficient decision evidence despite the chart's limited period and lack of causal or profitability evidence.
B.conditions: Assumes the displayed May–September observations are comparable, the axis labels correctly describe the measures, and a midyear association is sufficient for approval.
